findings.reason: with the last open followup f-araiid-028 ending at §34, §38 and §39 are reachable by no dispatch, so the plan cannot close on them and their dependence on §37 is invisible to any reader of the declarations.
findings.text: §38 and §39 are declared implementable but no open followup names either, and the `plan-section-depends-on` map carries only `s35→s33`, `s34→s36`, `s36→s37`, `s37→s35`; §38 states in prose "Build it after §37 merges, because §37 also writes `reckon/ledger.py`" and §39 "can be built beside it", so the ordering exists only in the sections' own bodies

findings.reason: the node's only measure would be a zero-stat assertion that holds on the unfixed tree, so the gate proves nothing while reading as green.
findings.text: the fixture is "a temporary project with at least 200 run files and one roster member", but `_crew_rows` computes `referenced_projects` from `crew.list_live()` and calls `ledger.load` only for a project that has a live pointer (`reckon/serve.py:1022-1025`); a fixture with run files and an aggregate member but no live pointer exercises no `ledger.load`, so the base revision also counts zero stats under `runs/` and "The assertion fails at the base revision" is unfalsifiable

findings.reason: the stated deduplication is the half of §39 that removes the duplicate load, and with no assertion for it a worker can land the helper and still ship the doubled poll.
findings.text: §39's Deliverable requires "The shell and the crew view share one `/crew` poll rather than running two", yet the done-when asserts only the helper's single-outstanding-request property and that the three files "start no `setInterval` that fetches"; two independent helper-scheduled pollers in `shell.jsx` and `crew.jsx` satisfy both assertions while leaving the duplicated `/crew` route the Why names as the defect ("a tab showing the crew view polls the same route twice per interval")

findings.reason: the measure admits the exact remedy the section's own evidence rejects, so a node could land an 81 MB read per 3 s poll and pass the gate §38 exists to impose.
findings.text: §38's Why states "Reading the aggregate directly is no remedy: reckon's crew.json is 81 MB", but its Deliverable permits a cost "bounded by the aggregate and the index", and the done-when measures only `stat` calls under `runs/`, which a full 81 MB aggregate read satisfies

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_crew_rows` resolves (`reckon/serve.py:1015`), `_file_identity` (`reckon/ledger.py:1028`), `_run_snapshot` (`reckon/ledger.py:1036`), `refreshRuns` (`docs/ui/shell.jsx:277`), the `plan.jsx` and `crew.jsx` pollers (`docs/ui/plan.jsx:627`, `docs/ui/crew.jsx:348`), `docs/ui/_shared.jsx` and `tests/test_spa_crew_cards.py` all exist; every `plan-section-depends-on` entry resolves to a section that exists.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §38's base-arm control cannot fire as the fixture is described (line 268), because `_crew_rows` reaches the stat-ing `ledger.load` only for a project with a live pointer (`reckon/serve.py:1022-1025`).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §34 writes to "the run's report directory", §38 and §39 put every log "under the run directory" and end it in EXIT=; none names a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new units name mechanism (`_crew_rows`, `_file_identity`, `refreshRuns`, `read_only_region`) and carry no version tag, ticket number or stage label into a symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §38's Why rejects reading the aggregate directly ("no remedy: reckon's crew.json is 81 MB", line 266) while its Deliverable permits a cost "bounded by the aggregate" and its done-when measures only `stat` counts, so the remedy the Why rejects satisfies the gate.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §34 is one measurement, §38 one read path, §39 one polling helper; the extra clauses in each are constraints on that one deliverable, not second deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §38 and §39 are both declared `implementable` (snapshot line 25) but appear in no followup body and in no `plan-section-depends-on` entry (line 9); the only open followup whose chain is still live, f-araiid-028 (lines 427–431), stops at §34.
